note.explanation: An element is identified by its atomic number, Z, which tells us how many protons its atoms have. The mass number, A, is the total number of protons and neutrons. Subtract Z from A to find the number of neutrons. In a neutral atom, electrons equal protons. For example, ¹⁶₈O has 8 protons, 8 electrons and 8 neutrons; ³²₁₆S has 16 neutrons.
note.checkAnswer: A neutral atom of ²³₁₁Na has 11 protons, 11 electrons and 12 neutrons.
note.simple: The atomic number gives the protons. The mass number gives protons plus neutrons. Subtract to find neutrons; in a neutral atom, electrons equal protons.

note.title: Atomic Number and Mass Number
steps: Read the left subscript: Z = number of protons.
For a neutral atom, set the number of electrons equal to the number of protons.
Read the left superscript: A = mass number.
Calculate neutrons using N = A − Z.
note.answer: Atomic number Z is the number of protons. Mass number A is the total number of protons and neutrons. Neutrons N = A − Z; electrons equal protons in a neutral atom.

explain.title: Atomic number
explain.body: The number of protons present in the atoms of an element is always fixed and it is called the atomic number of that element. It is represented by Z. An element is identified by its atomic number.

explain.title: Mass number
explain.body: The total number of protons and neutrons present in an atom almost accounts for the total mass of that atom and hence it is called its nucleon number or mass number. It is represented by A. The mass of electron being very small is not included in the mass number.

explain.title: Reading an atom symbol
explain.body: The atomic number is written as a left subscript while the mass number as a left superscript. For example, ¹⁶₈O has 8 protons and a mass number of 16.

explain.title: Finding neutrons
explain.body: The number of neutrons N present in an atom can be calculated if its atomic number Z and mass number (A) are known. N = A − Z. Since an atom as a whole is electrically neutral, the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

mistakes: Do not mix up the left superscript A (mass number) and left subscript Z (atomic number).
Do not use A + Z to find neutrons; use N = A − Z.
Do not say that the mass number includes electrons; it counts protons and neutrons.
For a neutral atom, do not make the electron count equal to the mass number; it equals the proton count.
